top.title: ‘Jalen Brunson wants…’ – Ex-WNBA star details why New York Knicks are struggling this season
top.description: Photo by David Berding/Getty Images Former WNBA player Chiney Ogwumike names the biggest problem for the New York Knicks. After the New York Knicks won the 2026 NBA Championship, fans expected a solid showing from the franchise in the 2026-27 season as well. However, this season hasn’t been kind to the Knicks, as they are currently the sixth seed in the Eastern Conference with a 9-6 record. As a result, fans are already starting to lose hope for a potential back-to-back NBA Championship run from the team. But what’s the reason behind the Knicks’ early-season struggles? Chiney Ogwumike says the New York Knicks need to change their ‘recipe’ Last season, the Knicks took teams by surprise with their tactics under head coach Mike Brown. Brown’s approach has remained relatively unchanged this season as well. According to former WNBA star Chiney Ogwumike, that’s where the problem lies for the defending NBA champions. “There’s no surprise factor anymore. Like everyone knows that this is a team that can beat anybody, the scouting report’s out, Jalen Brunson wants to close games and I think that you can’t use the same recipe and expect different results. The rest of the Eastern Conference is different. You sort of have to tweak some things,” Ogwumike began. “Now, I know it’s probably going to be sensitive with that starting lineup, but I would give them a little bit more time to sort of ease themselves into that possibility,” she further stated. In simple terms, the ESPN analyst wants coach Brown to experiment with different lineups and tactics, instead of relying on what worked last season. To be fair, the Knicks won the NBA title with those exact tactics, but the off-season has allowed other teams to be well-prepared for them, and the team’s 9-6 record is a perfect reflection of it. top.title: Bob Chesney reveals main message to UCLA amid CFP push
top.description: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images Bob Chesney reveals main message to UCLA amid CFP push appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The UCLA football Bruins have not been named a national champion since 1954. They have never won 11 games in a single campaign. They won just eight games combined across the previous two seasons. A 10-0 record carries significant weight for alumni, and top-four standing in the Playoff rankings carries even more. This program has completely transformed under Bob Chesney . But the head coach does not care about what the success represents, at least not right now. He is more concerned about how that success is achieved. Ahead of Saturday’s road game versus Michigan , Chesney is stressing the importance of ignoring all the outside praise. Hunger is fueled by a lack of satisfaction. He wants his players to be starving when they brave a rowdy Ann Arbor crowd that has nothing to celebrate except for a potential upset win versus a national title contender. “I said it back when we first got ranked. ‘Look, there’s a little number next to your name right now, and if you want to pay attention to that number, it will very quickly disappear. If you want to pay attention to how you got the number, and the process in which you did to earn that number, then who knows, maybe it could get a little bit better,'” the 2025 Sun Belt Coach of the Year (James Madison) said on SportsCenter with Scott Van Pelt. The next play is about to happen whether you like it or not. The next game is about to happen whether you like it or not, and you can’t let a previous success or failure determine our next success or failure.” Did you run through a brick wall yet? "We can't hold back and let a previous success or failure determine our next success or failure." UCLA head coach Bob Chesney joins @notthefakeSVP ahead of their game against Michigan and speaks on the message to his team 🏈 pic.twitter.com/he9W0NDtl9 — SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) November 21, 2026 Bob Chesney obviously has his players focused on the right things. UCLA football is rising at a meteoric pace , but it will instantly cool off with one loss versus a .500 Michigan squad. Keeping a locker room from getting too high or too low is an essential part of the job. And this man is clearly up to the task. The Bruins can reach that perpetually elusive 11th win, but they will hear Chesney’s “it doesn’t matter speech” if and when they reach that milestone. However, the school and fan base will certainly bask in that historic moment. UCLA-Michigan kicks off at about 3:30 p.m. ET on Saturday. top.title: “He is Such a Hypocrite”: Fans Torch Nick Saban as He Seemingly Changes Tack on Lane Kiffin’s Move to LSU from Ole Miss
top.description: Lane Kiffin and Nick Saban © Imagn Nick Saban was all for giving head coaches their due and supported Lane Kiffin when the former Ole Miss boss decided to head to LSU, but he has seemingly changed course after some poor performances this season for the Tigers. The former Alabama coach said that had Kiffin stayed at Ole Miss, he would have been able to build the team around Trinidad Chambliss. “I think if Lane Kiffin stayed at Ole Miss, they would have been able to build that team around Trinidad Chambliss…I respect Sam Leavitt as a competitor, and he makes a lot of plays…If you could just eliminate his bad plays, LSU would be in a completely different position,” Saban said on the Pat McAfee Show. Fans reacted to Saban’s comments, with one fan saying, “But Saban is the voice that was in Lane’s ear to leave Ole Miss for LSU. He is such a hypocrite. Saban can’t even give Pete Golding an ounce of credit.” Lane Kiffin Spoke About Returning to Tennessee As LSU prepares to play Tennessee on Saturday, Lane Kiffin was asked how it feels to play against his former team. Kiffin referred to the emotionally charged game against Ole Miss this season, when fans turned out in huge numbers to watch him return to his old stomping grounds. “I’m not challenging Tennessee, but I just don’t think you can top that (the atmosphere at Ole Miss),” Kiffin said , per USA Today. “Just the feeling of what that was like, and the anger and hatred, because it was so recent.” Kiffin coached Tennessee in 2009 and went 7-6 with the Vols before leaving to become head coach at USC. top.title: Steven Fakult leads Nordonia into OHSAA football state semifinal
top.description: TWINSBURG – The Nordonia football team completed its "Revenge Tour" on Friday, Nov. 20, in dramatic fashion. Senior quarterback Steven Fakult threw five touchdown passes, including one in overtime to senior Dominick Jackson in Nordonia's 35-28 win over Highland in the Division II, Region 5 championship at Twinsburg Tiger Stadium. “That’s what we practice,” Jackson said of the game-winning TD. “We have run that play a thousand times through my 10 years playing football here. So, we just had to put the emotion down and just do what we do best and just go make a play. … Steven is one my best buds. He's the greatest guy. People [at colleges] need to start taking more looks at him. He makes plays. He wins games.” Nordonia (12-1) advanced to play Columbus Bishop Watterson (12-0) in a state semifinal at 7 p.m. Friday, Nov. 27, at a site to be determined by the OHSAA. Nordonia is a state semifinalist for the first time since 2014 when it finished as Division II state runners-up. The Knights were also Division II state runners-up in 2002 and Division II state semifinalists in 2006. Watterson, the Division III state champion in 2024 and 2025, isn't part of the "Revenge Tour," but Highland (11-2) was. Nordonia’s path to a state semifinal included wins over the five teams that defeated the Knights since the start of last season. “You don't really get that many opportunities in high school football, so when you go out there you have to make the most of it, and we are fired up,” Jackson said. North Royalton, Wadsworth and Hudson beat Nordonia in the regular season in 2025, and Walsh Jesuit eliminated the Knights in a regional quarterfinal playoff game last season. Nordonia defeated Hudson, North Royalton and Wadsworth in the regular season in 2026, and eliminated Walsh Jesuit in a regional semifinal. Highland topped Nordonia 23-21 on Sept. 11 before the Knights reversed that outcome Friday in the postseason. “It all starts in the offseason,” Nordonia senior linebacker-running back-wide receiver Karsen Fisher said. “… So, this offseason it was all forget that — we are going to go beat your butt during this season, and we did that. Hudson and Wadsworth were the big ones. I had never beaten either of them until this season. "It was my personal duty to beat everybody we lost to. I made sure to keep the energy at practice, and this week especially with Highland. This is a regional freaking championship, man.” Jackson caught two of Fakult’s TD passes — a 35-yard strike in the second quarter and a 17-yard strike in overtime. Fakult threw a 27-yard TD pass to senior Grant Kaminski on a 4th-and-10 and a 5-yard TD pass to junior Jamison Elerick in the third quarter and a 1-yard TD pass to senior CJ Mayes on 4th-and-goal play. “We saw a cover 2, cover 4 type of defense, which is really kind of unorthodox for them,” Fakult said of the final TD pass to Jackson. “Usually it's been cover 3, cover 1. top.title: Skip Bayless names ‘the best player’ in the NFL right now
top.description: Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Skip Bayless has called Josh Allen the best player in the NFL while speaking about why he should be the MVP ahead of Joe Burrow. Allen previously won the award in 2024 and is in the midst of another impressive season with his Buffalo Bills 8-1 ahead of their Week 11 game. The Bills quarterback has some strong competition for the award this year, including from Joe Burrow. But while Bayless thinks the Cincinnati Bengals star is ‘the ultimate system quarterback’, he is of the opinion that ‘Allen has revolutionised’ the QB role and is ‘the best player in football and he should be the MVP’. Speaking on First Take, he said: “Josh Allen has revolutionised the quarterback position in ways I never thought I would see in my lifetime because he has scored 11 rushing touchdowns in the red zone. He’s become the Derrick Henry of quarterbacks. He is just simply unstoppable. “While Joe Burrow is the ultimate system quarterback, almost always throwing it on time, Josh Allen’s offence is mostly backyard. I think he makes up almost every play. He’s getting away with a running back who weighs 190 pounds running between the tackles. “It is all Josh Allen. He’s the best player in football and he should be the MVP.” How Josh Allen and Joe Burrow compare Allen currently has a better record with the Bills this season but Burrow does lead him in some key stats. The Bengals quarterback has the second-most passing yards in the NFL (2,795), which is considerably more than Josh (2,223). He also has a much higher completion rate (74.7%) compared to Allen (65.0%) and has more passing yards per game (310.6 vs 247.0). But as Bayless suggested, the Bills player is a pretty unique style of quarterback as he actually leads the league in rushing touchdowns (11) alongside Jahmyr Gibbs. Burrow is the joint-closest quarterback to matching Allen on that front but he only has three rushing touchdowns. It remains to be seen who will be crowned MVP this season but both players should still be in contention, and while Skip may be supporting Allen’s claim, others disagree. Among them is Tom Brady, who says it’s ‘pretty obvious’ Burrow is the best quarterback in the league. However, former Colts star Stephon Gilmore has pushed back against those criticisms, expressing confidence in Irsay-Gordon’s leadership. Gilmore defended the Colts owner on social media, saying he has personally seen her involved in team meetings and believes she understands football better than many give her credit for. “Yall have to chill on Carlie Irsay. I’ve seen her in meetings. She knows more ball than a lot of so-called football people. She’s very passionate about the game and the Colts. I’ve seen her in meetings. Analyst Blames Carlie Irsay-Gordon for Colts’ Collapse NFL analyst Michael Holley delivered a harsh assessment of Irsay-Gordon’s leadership on Pro Football Talk after the Houston loss. “This is gonna sound crazy. We were watching two three-win teams last night,” Holley said. He argued that the decision to fire general manager Chris Ballard and to trade away several key players derailed Indianapolis’ season. He continued questioning whether the coaching staff could still effectively manage players and end the season on a good note. The Colts have struggled significantly this season; against Houston, they recorded just 167 total yards. With the franchise facing questions about its direction, Irsay-Gordon has very little time to make changes and turn things around to silence the critics. top.title: Missing Newcastle United home matches
top.description: The Mag Pod Jamie Simon Hutch Watching Game St James' Park Newcastle United First off, I need to start with an apology to anyone coming to The Mag to read my report on whatever happens/has happened against Arsenal , I have decided to allow the editor to flex his squad strength due to my not being there today, missing Newcastle United home matches is, for me at least, a difficult business. I can already imagine some reading this are flabbergasted that someone with a ticket for a game against the Premier League champions would allow themselves to be otherwise occupied when they would crawl over broken all sorts to be there at any time. The thing is, I’m a bit of a victim of poor prediction skills, as a look at any of my recent accas will confirm. A few of my close mates were after arranging a meet up and a poll appeared in the WhatsApp group giving a choice of three weekends. One option was next week when I’m in Brighton, another was the untouchable territory of derby weekend and the remaining option was the Gunners at home. I took a punt and committed to this weekend, knowing that if the game was shifted to Sunday (or any other mad weekend kick off that wasn’t Saturday) I’d be able to get to it, convincing myself we’d be the Sunday warm up to Liverpool v Man Utd. So, it came to pass that wasn’t to be. So what do you do? Ditch your old mates and head to the game, or give someone else a chance with your ticket? Again, opinions will be polarised as some commentators will doubtless be about to say that they would chop their hand off with a rusty spoon to be in that ground, whereas many others will have found themselves in the position where they choose life over NUFC. I haven’t made this kind of miscalculation very often, with most of my absences from Newcastle United home matches being early season when it’s clashed with a holiday. Memories of enduring last season’s defeat to Liverpool in a bar at Disneyland Paris with an obnoxious cockney red mouthing off behind me are not amongst my most magical. It’s maybe a bit easier to swallow missing a defeat though. I’ll always remember when my youngest son was born and I confidently thought to myself he’d arrive in plenty of time for me to get to the game with Norwich in about six days. Mrs S saw it quite differently and her reaction to the prospect of me leaving her with a newborn and two toddlers as she recovered from a c-section was, if I’m honest, a bit over the top. I stayed at home and checked online to catch the news of Dwight Gayle’s 96th minute hat-trick goal sealing an incredible 4-3 comeback win. Honestly, during the whole Mike Ashley era it was a bit easier to give things a swerve. I remember hauling myself out of the house on a freezing Wednesday evening full of cold. top.title: PREVIEW | Werder Bremen and Hamburg prepare for Nordderby battle
top.description: PREVIEW | Werder Bremen and Hamburg prepare for Nordderby battle One of German football’s most historic rivalries returns this Sunday as Werder Bremen host Hamburg at the Weserstadion in the 111th Bundesliga edition of the Nordderby. With just three points separating the two clubs, the encounter promises to be one of Matchday 10’s most fascinating fixtures. Bremen enter the match sixth with 15 points, while Hamburg sit 11th with 12. Both clubs have enjoyed encouraging spells this season, making the derby particularly significant beyond their historic rivalry. Bremen’s home advantage and Füllkrug’s influence Daniel Thioune – who signed an extension 24 hours prior to the derby – has transformed Bremen into a more competitive side, with their seven-match unbeaten run ending against VfB Stuttgart before the international break. The Weserstadion has become a major advantage. Bremen remain unbeaten there this season, collecting 10 points from four matches. Niclas Füllkrug has been instrumental in their resurgence, scoring nine Bundesliga goals in nine appearances. Hamburg, meanwhile, have struggled away from home, losing four of their five matches on the road. However, their recent 3-1 victory over Borussia Mönchengladbach demonstrated their attacking potential, particularly through Miro Muheim’s dangerous long-range shooting. More than just three points The Nordderby also presents an intriguing managerial storyline. Thioune previously coached Hamburg and worked alongside current Hamburg head coach Merlin Polzin at Osnabrück before their paths crossed again in Hamburg. History favours Bremen, who have won eight of their previous nine Bundesliga home encounters against their northern rivals. Last season, however, both clubs won their respective home derbies, highlighting the unpredictable nature of this fixture. For Bremen, victory would reinforce their European ambitions and demonstrate that their impressive start is sustainable. Hamburg, meanwhile, have an opportunity to move level on points with their rivals and strengthen their position in the Bundesliga. Regardless of their respective league positions, the Nordderby represents something much bigger than three points. It is a contest shaped by history, regional pride and the desire to establish supremacy in northern Germany. With both teams showing encouraging signs this season, Sunday’s encounter has all the ingredients to deliver another memorable chapter in one of the Bundesliga’s greatest rivalries. GGFN | Felipe

top.title: LPGA Tour introduce ‘aggressive’ new solution to stop slow play
top.description: Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images The LPGA Tour is tackling pace of play head-on. It’s one of the biggest issues fans have with the modern game, as players are often taking around six hours to complete their rounds. And while the PGA Tour has often been criticized for not taking action to speed up the pace of play, the LPGA Tour is attempting to find solutions. Their latest move is to fine any player who has been put on the clock over 35 times in a year $35,000. That’s an extreme measure, considering the previous threshold was 40 holes, and the previous fine was $5,000. Under the new policy, the maximum time allowed for a single shot also drops from 70 seconds to 60 seconds, and players will pay $2,000 for a first offense, $4,000 for a second, and $8,000 for a third. Delays of six to 15 seconds still bring a one-stroke penalty plus a fine, while delays of 16 seconds or more carry a two-stroke penalty and a fine. LPGA Tour Commissioner Craig Kessler explained how the tour came to this new policy. LPGA Tour Commissioner explains new pace of play policy This new pace-of-play policy is a positive step for the LPGA Tour as it looks to speed up the game, and what’s even more encouraging is that the players are also invested in fixing the issue. How do we know that? Well, the players came up with the solution in the first place. That’s according to Kessler, who said on SiriusXM Radio: “The good news is we started with our fans, and the insight from fans is that pace of play matters. Fans want to see us play faster. We brought that to our players, and we actually have a pace-of-play committee. “And the beautiful thing here is it’s the players who developed the policy. They’re the ones that we understand the importance of playing faster. We understand what are the levers that we can pull to help bring that to life. “And they’re the ones who created the policy that we rolled out to frankly, a decent amount of applause from our players on Tuesday. “I’m very excited to see the policy implemented. If it works as intended, fantastic, and of course if we need to learn and adapt as we go then we’ll do just that.” This isn’t the only step the LPGA Tour has taken. nigeria.title: The Governor, The Candidate And The Voter
nigeria.description: Anambra puts the power of endorsements to the test, while opposition negotiations and election safeguards face approaching deadlines. On Thursday in Awka, Governor Chukwuma Soludo presented APGA’s flag to Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who received it on behalf of President Bola Tinubu. On Friday, Peter Obi took his campaign through Onitsha, attracting supporters ahead of his town hall engagement. Two neighbouring cities offered competing pictures of political strength. In Awka, the message was partnership with the centre. In Onitsha, Obi demonstrated his continuing ability to mobilise in the state he once governed. The electoral question lies between those pictures: how far can a governor’s endorsement move presidential votes, and how effectively can a candidate convert personal loyalty into turnout? Anambra will help answer both. Soludo’s Wager APGA’s support gives Tinubu an organised partner outside the APC. Soludo is making an argument about the South-East’s place in national politics: that cooperation with the President offers a route to influence and development. The presentation reaffirmed APGA’s presidential alignment while the party continues pursuing its own interests in other elections. For Tinubu, the opportunity lies in improving his reach through a political organisation rooted in the state. For Soludo, the challenge is to persuade people who support his governorship to make the same choice in a presidential contest. Those loyalties need not coincide. Voters can approve of a governor’s performance and prefer another presidential candidate. They can also reconsider a previous choice if a new alliance offers a convincing case. The evidence will emerge through sustained mobilisation, local organisation and ultimately the ballot. A flag presentation establishes an endorsement. It cannot establish the electorate’s response. Obi’s Home-State Test Obi’s Onitsha road show supplies evidence of campaign activity and visible support. It does not, on its own, measure the balance of opinion across Anambra. His task is to maintain that support while building sufficient reach elsewhere. The home-state contest also brings his governing record into sharper focus. nigeria.title: 11 dead, over 180 hospitalised after drinking alcohol
nigeria.description: At least 11 people have died and more than 180 have been hospitalised after drinking suspected tainted alcohol in India’s northeastern state of Manipur. The victims fell ill after consuming the liquor, Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh said in a statement on Friday. “Over 180 patients have been admitted in the two hospitals so far, while the death toll has reached 11 in the last 48 hours,” the statement said. He also ordered an enquiry into the incident, saying those responsible would be arrested and punished. Deaths from illicit or adulterated alcohol are regularly reported in India, where cheap liquor sold outside regulated channels can contain methanol, a highly toxic industrial chemical. In May, at least 15 people died after drinking methanol-laced illicit liquor in Pune and neighbouring Pimpri-Chinchwad in the western state of Maharashtra. In August, 13 people died and more than 60 were affected after consuming methanol-tainted liquor in Gujarat’s Bhavnagar district, according to local media reports. Such liquor is widely consumed across India, where a bottle is sometimes sold for less than a dollar. If ingested, methanol can cause blindness, liver damage and death in larger concentrations. Twenty-four other passengers were rescued following the incident, which occurred at about 11am while the boat was travelling from Ayama community to Ukubie. The Bayelsa State Police Command said preliminary findings indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways. The police spokesperson, Musa Mohammed, disclosed this in a statement on Friday, alleging that some passengers had urged the operator to steer towards the riverbank after the fault developed, but he declined and continued the journey before the boat capsized. Mohammed said the bodies of two adults and two children had been recovered and deposited at the mortuary of the Federal Medical Centre, Yenagoa. He said 24 survivors were rescued, with 19 taken to Ayama Clinic, while five others who sustained injuries were transferred to Family Care Hospital in Yenagoa for treatment. The police spokesperson disclosed that the boat operator, identified only as Omovie, had fled the scene, while the boat manager, identified as MV Bina, had been taken into custody for investigation. He added that the police marine section had been deployed to reinforce search and rescue operations, while the Divisional Police Officer in Oporoma was coordinating efforts with local divers and other emergency responders. Mohammed said investigations were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the tragedy, assuring that search and rescue operations would continue until everyone on board had been accounted for. business.title: SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme The Securities and Exchange Commission has frozen the assets of Indianapolis-based Backward Hat Capital and its two co-founders, saying the firm ran a $560 million Ponzi scheme that told investors their money would be turned into crypto and used for AI-driven currency trading. The agency said Backward Hat, co-founders Phillip Williams and Devin Johnson, Johnson’s firm Traders Point Capital and Joseph Anderson raised the money from more than 2,000 investors starting in July 2022. A federal court granted a temporary restraining order, an asset freeze and expedited discovery to halt what the SEC called an ongoing scheme. Federal prosecutors in New York and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission brought parallel cases. The SEC and CFTC suits were filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, and the CFTC said the court has appointed Kevin B. Duff as temporary receiver to take control of the companies and the individual defendants’ assets. The pitch: crypto, AI and 6% a month According to the SEC’s complaint , Williams and Johnson sold limited partnership interests in private funds through a network of promoters, including to Williams’s former investment advisory clients. They promised a proprietary, “AI-driven” algorithm that supposedly returned at least 6% every month by trading foreign exchange. Investor money, the pitch went, would first be converted into a crypto asset and then used for that arbitrage. The complaint does not name bitcoin as the asset. It says about $109 million of the roughly $210 million raised from July 2022 to September 2025 was sent to the fund’s Coinbase account and converted. Of that, more than $56 million went to personal crypto accounts held by Williams, Johnson and a relief defendant, according to the complaint. About $40 million ended up on three platforms where some of it was used to trade other crypto assets, but little to no money was used to trade FX. After October 2025, the scheme raised about $350 million, and none of it was sent to Coinbase. Where the money went The SEC said the defendants made more than $250 million in Ponzi payments to earlier investors and moved more than $220 million to themselves. The money paid for exotic cars, expensive homes, private air travel and other businesses they owned, and helped feed Johnson’s gambling. Promoters took more than $50 million. Anderson is accused of producing fake financial reports, including at least two “audit reports” and a “quality of earnings” report from a supposedly independent firm. The SEC said the documents falsely claimed the returns had been verified against bank and brokerage records. It said Anderson did no audit work, was not independent and had a financial stake in the scheme. entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. Held at the Balmoral Convention Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos, the ceremony brought together young achievers, industry leaders and public figures to celebrate two decades of recognizing African excellence. Themed “ Celebrating the Redefiners: Africa’s AI Generation,” the evening honoured young Africans aged 18 to 35 across 26 categories, including technology and innovation, entrepreneurship, governance, music, film, literature, advocacy, sports and fashion. Their achievements formed the heart of a milestone edition that celebrated the platform’s legacy while embracing new possibilities for its stage. Together, the five hosts gave the anniversary celebration a distinctly continental presence. Bringing different voices, personalities and perspectives to the proceedings, the line-up reflected the reach of an awards platform whose story has grown alongside the generations of young Africans it recognises. entertainment.description: One of the best aspects of art is its ability to imitate current events or imagine possibilities. Movies, as a powerful art form, present a sequence of events that allows viewers to see reflections of themselves or envision who they could become. At its core, art exists to entertain, inform and critique society. Through films, music and visual expressions, we are continually reminded of our shared humanity—our joys, flaws and contradictions. One subject that art, particularly film, has explored is masculinity. However, this theme is often addressed subtly and can be easy to overlook, as the movies that dominate global box offices frequently focus on spectacle: fantasy, romance, adventure or others. Conversations about men, their inner lives, vulnerabilities and social roles are often not in the top circle. Nonetheless, some films have attempted to explore what it means to be a man in today’s world. They invite audiences to contemplate important questions such as: What is the role of men in society? What defines a man? How does a man’s behaviour influence those around him? What expectations does society place on men? What responsibilities do men have within society? Through his struggles with homelessness, rejection, and exhaustion, the film redefines masculinity, depicting it as the courage to remain tender even when life tests your strength in every way. entertainment.description: What does it really mean to play to win in business and leadership? Beyond earning a seat at the table, it requires more than competence or professional accomplishments. It requires the confidence to own one’s value, the clarity to communicate one’s contributions and the intentionality to build visibility that translates into meaningful influence. These conversations defined The Executive Woman Summit (TEWS) 2.0 , which brought together hundreds of executive women, corporate professionals, entrepreneurs and emerging leaders at Harbour Point, Victoria Island, Lagos, on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. Convened by Bola Matel-Okoh , a dual-qualified attorney (called to both the New York and Nigerian Bars), Executive Coach, Non-Executive Director at Wema Bank, and CEO of BMO Advisory Services , the second edition of the summit was themed Playing to Win: Elevate Your Vision, Value and Visibility. It provided an intentional platform for candid conversations, practical insights and strategic alliances on what it takes for women to advance, lead and thrive in today’s evolving corporate landscape. In her opening address, Matel-Okoh challenged women to rethink how they approach professional visibility, authority and advancement. According to her, competence is merely the baseline; it is not enough if you are unwilling to communicate your value, own your voice and position yourself for higher-stakes opportunities. This philosophy also came through in her cover interview with THISDAY Glitterati ahead of the summit, where she offered a compelling perspective on the distinction between holding a powerful position and exercising genuine influence. “A powerful position gives you formal authority. Influence determines how deeply your leadership shapes people’s thinking, decisions and actions. A title may secure your place in a meeting, but credibility makes people listen,” she explained. She also challenged the assumption that excellent work will automatically speak for itself, encouraging women to communicate their contributions with evidence and confidence. “What problem did you solve? What result did you produce? What changed because of your leadership?” she asked, highlighting the importance of making professional value visible to the decision-makers who influence career progression and boardroom opportunities. “There is no need to diminish your achievements to make others comfortable. You can be gracious and still be clear about the value you bring,” she added. entertainment.title: Tochukwu Ekoh: What My Friend’s Passing Taught Me About Kindness
entertainment.description: A thoughtful young woman sits in a relaxed pose in a serene bedroom, reflecting peacefully. Photo credit: Alex Green/Pexels. I lost someone recently, and since then, I have found myself revisiting little moments, conversations and encounters I probably would not have given much thought to otherwise. We weren’t particularly close , or I wouldn’t describe our relationship that way . We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Beyond the guilt, there was another question I couldn’t get out of my head: Why did God allow us to reconnect? Why, after such a long time, did our paths have to cross again? Why did we have to start talking, sharing experiences and becoming familiar with each other again, only for him to die shortly afterwards? Why him? Why at that particular time? What was the reason for that reconnection, and why did it have to end this way? The timing of certain events leaves you with more questions than answers. What makes this loss even more difficult to comprehend is how it happened. I had been the one who suffered an accident, yet I survived and was gradually recovering. He wasn’t sick. entertainment.title: Entertainment Week Africa officially kicks Off 5th Edition in Lagos | November 17th – 22nd
entertainment.description: Entertainment Week Africa (EWA) , the pan-African platform for the business of creativity, opens its fifth edition in Lagos tomorrow, Wednesday, 18 November. The programme runs until Saturday, 21 November, and brings together creators, executives, investors, policymakers and delegations from more than 18 African countries. This year’s theme, Five Years of Closing the Gap, reflects the purpose EWA was built around: connecting African talent with the capital, markets, skills and audiences it needs to grow. Since its first edition, EWA has welcomed more than 67,800 attendees. The 2025 edition alone recorded 28,683 pass-holders from over eight countries and 50 industries, across 61 sessions, 93 film screenings, 20 music showcases and nine fashion showcases. By day and by night The week runs across two venues. By day, EbonyLife Place on Victoria Island hosts panels, roundtables, workshops, masterclasses, and film screenings. By night, the programme moves to the Livespot Entertarium in Ikate, beginning with Opening Night on 18 November at 6pm, an evening of music, fashion, film, comedy and awards. The Entertarium also houses the week’s experiences, including an exhibition, the EWA Art Floor, a fashion show, comedy, live music, a beauty exhibition and a marketplace. Seven tracks, one market The 2026 programme is organised across seven tracks: Film & TV; Music; Fashion & Beauty; AI & Tech; Live Events & Production; Creative Enterprise; and Art & Animation, which is new this year. Alongside the conference, EWA runs a set of commercial formats designed to move deals forward. They include the EWA Deal Room, the Content and Music Markets, the EWA Capital Desk, the Creators Hub and LABSPOT, EWA’s skills and enterprise development engine. Last year’s Deal Room received more than 178 entries and advanced nine companies to its accelerator, with Future Africa, Catalyst Fund, Consonance Invest and Askya Investment Partners among the participating investors and partners. Between 30 and 40 per cent of this year’s delegates are expected to travel from outside Nigeria, with delegations from Kenya, Rwanda, Ghana, Senegal, Uganda, Tanzania and South Africa among them. The edition will also host the exclusive screening of University of Side Hustle, the first scripted feature film from Livespot Studios, written by Dami Elebe , executive produced by Deola Art Alade. entertainment.title: Visa Report Identifies Opportunity to Integrate Digital Payments with SMEs Business Operations in Nigeria
entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. entertainment.description: Sade Adu in the Performer category and Fela Kuti in the Early Influence category, both inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Class of 2026. Nigerian music history just added another major chapter in Los Angeles, and the celebration has been loud from Lagos to London. On Saturday, 14 November 2026, Afrobeat pioneer Fela Aníkúlápó Kuti and Nigerian-British singer Sade Adu were officially inducted into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame during a star-studded ceremony at the Peacock Theatre. For Fela Kuti, nearly three decades after his passing in 1997, this induction makes him the first African-born solo artist to enter the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Honoured posthumously in the Early Influence category—five years after he was first nominated in 2021—the recognition celebrates how he fused West African rhythms with jazz, funk, and soul to create Afrobeat, using his voice and horns to confront social and political injustice across classics like “Zombie”, “Water No Get Enemy”, and “Sorrow, Tears and Blood”. It also caps off an extraordinary 2026 for his legacy, coming just months after the Recording Academy presented him with a posthumous Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award in February, another first for an African artist. From left, Made Kuti, Femi Kuti, Yeni Kuti, and Seun Kuti in Los Angeles for Fela Aníkúlápó Kuti’s posthumous induction into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Speaking on the milestone, the family reflected on how remarkable it is to see Fela receive both the Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award and a Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction in the very same year. Meanwhile, Sade Adu —born Helen Folasade Adu in Ibadan—was inducted in th e Performer category as the frontwoman of her acclaimed British band Sade , alongside longtime bandmates Stuart Matthewman , Paul Spencer Denman , and Andrew Hale . sports.title: ‘Jalen Brunson wants…’ – Ex-WNBA star details why New York Knicks are struggling this season
sports.description: Photo by David Berding/Getty Images Former WNBA player Chiney Ogwumike names the biggest problem for the New York Knicks. After the New York Knicks won the 2026 NBA Championship, fans expected a solid showing from the franchise in the 2026-27 season as well. However, this season hasn’t been kind to the Knicks, as they are currently the sixth seed in the Eastern Conference with a 9-6 record. As a result, fans are already starting to lose hope for a potential back-to-back NBA Championship run from the team. But what’s the reason behind the Knicks’ early-season struggles? Chiney Ogwumike says the New York Knicks need to change their ‘recipe’ Last season, the Knicks took teams by surprise with their tactics under head coach Mike Brown. Brown’s approach has remained relatively unchanged this season as well. According to former WNBA star Chiney Ogwumike, that’s where the problem lies for the defending NBA champions. “There’s no surprise factor anymore. Like everyone knows that this is a team that can beat anybody, the scouting report’s out, Jalen Brunson wants to close games and I think that you can’t use the same recipe and expect different results. The rest of the Eastern Conference is different. You sort of have to tweak some things,” Ogwumike began. “Now, I know it’s probably going to be sensitive with that starting lineup, but I would give them a little bit more time to sort of ease themselves into that possibility,” she further stated. In simple terms, the ESPN analyst wants coach Brown to experiment with different lineups and tactics, instead of relying on what worked last season. To be fair, the Knicks won the NBA title with those exact tactics, but the off-season has allowed other teams to be well-prepared for them, and the team’s 9-6 record is a perfect reflection of it. The UCLA football Bruins have not been named a national champion since 1954. They have never won 11 games in a single campaign. They won just eight games combined across the previous two seasons. A 10-0 record carries significant weight for alumni, and top-four standing in the Playoff rankings carries even more. This program has completely transformed under Bob Chesney . I made sure to keep the energy at practice, and this week especially with Highland. sports.description: Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Skip Bayless has called Josh Allen the best player in the NFL while speaking about why he should be the MVP ahead of Joe Burrow. Allen previously won the award in 2024 and is in the midst of another impressive season with his Buffalo Bills 8-1 ahead of their Week 11 game. The Bills quarterback has some strong competition for the award this year, including from Joe Burrow. But while Bayless thinks the Cincinnati Bengals star is ‘the ultimate system quarterback’, he is of the opinion that ‘Allen has revolutionised’ the QB role and is ‘the best player in football and he should be the MVP’. Speaking on First Take, he said: “Josh Allen has revolutionised the quarterback position in ways I never thought I would see in my lifetime because he has scored 11 rushing touchdowns in the red zone. He’s become the Derrick Henry of quarterbacks. He is just simply unstoppable. “While Joe Burrow is the ultimate system quarterback, almost always throwing it on time, Josh Allen’s offence is mostly backyard. I think he makes up almost every play. He’s getting away with a running back who weighs 190 pounds running between the tackles. “It is all Josh Allen. He’s the best player in football and he should be the MVP.” How Josh Allen and Joe Burrow compare Allen currently has a better record with the Bills this season but Burrow does lead him in some key stats. The Bengals quarterback has the second-most passing yards in the NFL (2,795), which is considerably more than Josh (2,223). He also has a much higher completion rate (74.7%) compared to Allen (65.0%) and has more passing yards per game (310.6 vs 247.0). But as Bayless suggested, the Bills player is a pretty unique style of quarterback as he actually leads the league in rushing touchdowns (11) alongside Jahmyr Gibbs. Burrow is the joint-closest quarterback to matching Allen on that front but he only has three rushing touchdowns. It remains to be seen who will be crowned MVP this season but both players should still be in contention, and while Skip may be supporting Allen’s claim, others disagree. sports.description: PREVIEW | Werder Bremen and Hamburg prepare for Nordderby battle One of German football’s most historic rivalries returns this Sunday as Werder Bremen host Hamburg at the Weserstadion in the 111th Bundesliga edition of the Nordderby. With just three points separating the two clubs, the encounter promises to be one of Matchday 10’s most fascinating fixtures. Bremen enter the match sixth with 15 points, while Hamburg sit 11th with 12. Both clubs have enjoyed encouraging spells this season, making the derby particularly significant beyond their historic rivalry. Bremen’s home advantage and Füllkrug’s influence Daniel Thioune – who signed an extension 24 hours prior to the derby – has transformed Bremen into a more competitive side, with their seven-match unbeaten run ending against VfB Stuttgart before the international break. The Weserstadion has become a major advantage. Bremen remain unbeaten there this season, collecting 10 points from four matches. Niclas Füllkrug has been instrumental in their resurgence, scoring nine Bundesliga goals in nine appearances. Hamburg, meanwhile, have struggled away from home, losing four of their five matches on the road. However, their recent 3-1 victory over Borussia Mönchengladbach demonstrated their attacking potential, particularly through Miro Muheim’s dangerous long-range shooting. More than just three points The Nordderby also presents an intriguing managerial storyline. Thioune previously coached Hamburg and worked alongside current Hamburg head coach Merlin Polzin at Osnabrück before their paths crossed again in Hamburg. History favours Bremen, who have won eight of their previous nine Bundesliga home encounters against their northern rivals. Last season, however, both clubs won their respective home derbies, highlighting the unpredictable nature of this fixture. For Bremen, victory would reinforce their European ambitions and demonstrate that their impressive start is sustainable. Hamburg, meanwhile, have an opportunity to move level on points with their rivals and strengthen their position in the Bundesliga. Regardless of their respective league positions, the Nordderby represents something much bigger than three points. It is a contest shaped by history, regional pride and the desire to establish supremacy in northern Germany. sports.title: LPGA Tour introduce ‘aggressive’ new solution to stop slow play
sports.description: Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images The LPGA Tour is tackling pace of play head-on. It’s one of the biggest issues fans have with the modern game, as players are often taking around six hours to complete their rounds. And while the PGA Tour has often been criticized for not taking action to speed up the pace of play, the LPGA Tour is attempting to find solutions. Their latest move is to fine any player who has been put on the clock over 35 times in a year $35,000. That’s an extreme measure, considering the previous threshold was 40 holes, and the previous fine was $5,000. Under the new policy, the maximum time allowed for a single shot also drops from 70 seconds to 60 seconds, and players will pay $2,000 for a first offense, $4,000 for a second, and $8,000 for a third. Delays of six to 15 seconds still bring a one-stroke penalty plus a fine, while delays of 16 seconds or more carry a two-stroke penalty and a fine. LPGA Tour Commissioner Craig Kessler explained how the tour came to this new policy. LPGA Tour Commissioner explains new pace of play policy This new pace-of-play policy is a positive step for the LPGA Tour as it looks to speed up the game, and what’s even more encouraging is that the players are also invested in fixing the issue. How do we know that? Well, the players came up with the solution in the first place. That’s according to Kessler, who said on SiriusXM Radio: “The good news is we started with our fans, and the insight from fans is that pace of play matters. Fans want to see us play faster. We brought that to our players, and we actually have a pace-of-play committee. “And the beautiful thing here is it’s the players who developed the policy. They’re the ones that we understand the importance of playing faster. We understand what are the levers that we can pull to help bring that to life. “And they’re the ones who created the policy that we rolled out to frankly, a decent amount of applause from our players on Tuesday. “I’m very excited to see the policy implemented. If it works as intended, fantastic, and of course if we need to learn and adapt as we go then we’ll do just that.” This isn’t the only step the LPGA Tour has taken. Unlike the PGA Tour, the LPGA has enforced two-stroke penalties on players this season, taking action on Yealimi Noh and Carlota Ciganda and ultimately costing them victories. technology.title: NASA Mars rover and orbiter suffer glitches
technology.description: It's been a bad few weeks for technology on and off the planet, as NASA reported problems with its Perseverance Mars rover and Odyssey orbiter this week. For Perseverance, the problem seems to be a relatively straightforward communications issue that has paused science operations because of low data rates. The Odyssey orbiter, however, is facing an issue that could end the mission. The 2001 Mars Odyssey reached orbit around Mars in October 2001 to search for evidence of water and ice on the surface. The mission was supposed to last two and a half years, but the spacecraft's operations have been extended for a quarter of a century. In that time, it has had its fair share of ups and downs, including the failure of one of its four reaction wheels in 2013. Three reaction wheels are needed to orient the spacecraft; otherwise, it must fall back to its hydrazine thrusters. Earlier in November, between the 4th and 6th, Odyssey dropped into safe mode, which engineers determined was caused by one of the remaining reaction wheels stopping spinning. Science data stopped flowing as the team worked to recover the component; the good news was that the wheel moved when commanded. The bad news is that if the thrusters need to be used, only a few months of fuel remain. More bad news is that the spacecraft is part of NASA's Mars Relay Network, and was responsible for sending back the first post-landing images from the Phoenix lander and the Spirit, Opportunity, and Curiosity rovers. Its loss (should it come to that) would therefore be keenly felt. In the event the orbiter is indeed approaching the end of the road, the European Space Agency's Mars Express (MEX) and Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO) could pick up some of the load although, as a former ESA insider put it: "MEX is a science mission that can do relay where TGO is a relay mission that also does science." According to NASA, TGO already sends the most relay data from Mars to Earth. The challenge facing the Perseverance trundlebot is one of communication. On October 30, the rover's main computer detected problems with the primary radio (a series of "heartbeats" from the device did not arrive as expected) and automatically switched to a redundant backup, placing itself in a protective safe mode. So far, so expected. Engineers brought the rover back from safe mode, analyzed the data, and made an unpleasant discovery. The backup radio was not performing as it should – it was operating at approximately half of its expected power output. Both radios were therefore deemed inoperable – at least until the team has got to the bottom of the issues – and the rover has used X-band communications over its high-gain antenna to talk to Earth ever since. The problem here is that the connection provides a significantly lower data rate, meaning science and instrument operations are on hold. Engineers are working first to return the backup radio to operational status, then to address the primary. ®

technology.title: PHP 8.6: Things are gonna get a lot more strict around here
technology.description: On Thursday, PHP version 8.6 was released on its usual yearly schedule, popping up as if the web scripting language hadn’t been under intense scrutiny this past month. For those who missed it: a swarm of unearthed vulnerabilities has plagued PHP since October, allowing unauthenticated attackers to crash PHP workers or execute arbitrary code on the server. Users of every PHP-based application, including WordPress, Laravel, and Symfony, had to scramble to update their PHP instances. The PHP core development community, along with the PHP Foundation , responded with a coordinated release of patched versions of PHP ( 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, 8.2.36 and the new 8.6) that closed seven critical remote code execution (RCE) flaws in one sweep. In addition to patching specific exploitable holes in the PHP engine, the new version of PHP also tamps down some of PHP’s historically liberal configuration settings. Lucky for PHP, and for the rest of us, core developer Jörg Sowa called out these lax settings in June, when he posted a proposal to set more security-friendly defaults. Sowa saw that three configuration settings of PHP’s session extension – Strict Mode, HttpOnly, and SameSite – were designed to boost security but shipped “with defaults that leave applications unnecessarily exposed.” No cookies for impostors In a retrospective posted last month, the PHP Foundation admitted that consensus-driven gridlock had stalled complex fixes for months and vowed to get patches out the door sooner, should the vulnerabilities leak ahead of the agreed-upon deadline . Code-wise, Sowa’s proposal to harden PHP settings was accepted for PHP 8.6. These changes won’t stop the flood of AI-generated CVEs, but at least these holes will be more difficult to exploit. For Strict Mode, PHP will no longer accept uninitialized session IDs that it didn’t create itself. Before, an attacker could just plant a made-up session ID on the victim to gain entry. “The built-in files handler checks whether a session file for that ID exists on disk; because an attacker-planted ID has no corresponding file, a fresh random ID is generated instead,” Sowa wrote. Furthermore, PHP will now, by default, add the HttpOnly flag to its session Set-Cookie header, blocking client-side JavaScript from reading the session ID, which could otherwise be stolen to masquerade as the user. Believe it or not, any script on the page could read it before. Finally, the server will withhold session cookies on cross-site POST requests, as well as for subrequests and iframes. “Without it, a forged form or link on an attacker-controlled site can trigger authenticated requests using the victim’s session,” Sowa wrote. Going forward, cookies will only be sent on same-site requests and top-level GET navigations, such as clicking a normal link. technology.title: Visa, Mastercard theft included info useful for phishing, but not draining bank accounts, say researchers
technology.description: Visa and Mastercard customer info leaked by the data thieves and extortionists who claim to have stolen it from the financial giants doesn’t include card numbers, passwords, or home addresses. On Thursday, Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan Chase confirmed to The Register that they are investigating third-party breaches that may involve customer information. Ransomware and extortion crew n0n claimed to be responsible for all three, and on Thursday published samples of the stolen files – data-theft groups typically leak some of the compromised data ahead of the official extortion deadline in an effort to put more pressure on victim companies to pay the ransom demand. Researchers at SOCRadar, a threat-intelligence firm that has been tracking n0n since it emerged in September, have parsed all 14 files in the n0n’s published Visa and Mastercard archives, and told us that the files don’t contain any financial details belonging to banking customers. “We found no card numbers, expiry dates, CVVs, passwords, dates of birth, or home addresses in any file,” Ensar Seker, SOCRadar chief information security officer, told The Register . “Visa's statement that no card numbers were affected matches our scan.” Mastercard previously said that stolen data included a “limited amount of email addresses – non-payments information” from a subset of cardholders in a benefits program. According to SOCRadar’s analysis, the leaked files do contain mobile numbers, Bank Identification Number (BIN) prefixes, and dated airline, hotel, and restaurant bookings. So while the data doesn’t include card or account numbers that crooks could use to drain customers' bank accounts or rack up massive credit card bills, “that detail is what a fraudster needs to pose as a concierge desk or a bank,” in an email or voice-phishing social engineering attack, Seker said. It’s also worth noting that the published files only represent about 0.4 percent of the data n0n claims to have hoovered up in the breach: about 4.3 GB and 1.9 million marketing events. “So a further release is possible,” according to Seker. Plus, both datasets come from the same upstream provider, we’re told. They use the same 27-column booking layout, placeholder text, and CRM ID format, Seker said, noting that the most recent record in each stops 69 seconds apart on Oct 26. “This looks like two card programs run on one provider's platform,” he said. “The pattern looks like a batch copy from a marketing and reporting store.” Customer data has left the building The security shop hasn’t analyzed the Chase customer data that n0n also claimed to have published. technology.title: Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.
technology.description: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve. The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model. Security breaches, prompt theft, and privacy violations To test for potential leakage, researcher HD Moore assembled a collection of Amazon Web Services access keys, functioning credentials tied to empty AWS accounts, passwords for services such as SSH, and unique URLs, DNS names, and private git repository references. None of the secrets had ever been used before, and he controlled the infrastructure that received any requests using the credentials. He then seeded each secret into exactly one prompt sent to a single provider. In the event any of the secrets were leaked, these “canaries”—so called because they resemble the role of that bird when taken into coal mines—would allow Moore to identify each link in the chain that was responsible. technology.title: Signal slams door on prying AI agents to protect privacy
technology.description: Signal, the encrypted messaging app, has barred Google Gemini, Apple Siri, and other AI agents from accessing messages unless the user has explicitly granted permission, based on privacy concerns. Citing the screenshot blocking implemented last year to defend against Microsoft Recall, Signal CEO Meredith Whittaker said similar measures have become necessary to prevent agentic software available in iOS and Android from gaining access to communication that's intended to be private. "Google and Apple are integrating agentic capabilities like Gemini Intelligence with Google Gemini and Onscreen Awareness with Siri AI deep into their operating systems," wrote Whittaker in a blog post . "In order to gain access to information about you, these OS AI agents 'scan' the information that’s on your screen. In doing so, your Signal data is captured, then made available to these agentic systems in order to allow them to answer your questions and do your bidding." The result is that private messages ingested by these agentic systems may end up on someone else's server where they're no longer private. Updates to Signal's iOS and Android apps now include controls that by default block Siri on iOS and Gemini and other agents on Android from taking screenshots, which AI agents process using optical character recognition to extract text. Whittaker says that those who wish to take screenshots of their messages can disable this protection via Signal's settings menu, but warns doing so risks exposing your Signal content (and that sent by your contacts) to AI agents. Screenshot blocking, Whittaker concedes, is only a partial solution since AI agents may have other ways to access application data through the device file system. "We want to be very clear: it is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy," she said. "Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft, and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience. This is also the reason we are currently unable to implement these protections on macOS." Apple is taking some action to implement protection from AI agents on macOS, though it appears to be doing so largely to defend against third-party access to data rather than to limit its own Siri service. Siri can be turned off separately. With macOS 27.3 , currently in public beta testing, Apple's desktop operating system will get more granular controls on two APIs: Device Control and Data Access, and Full Disk Access. technology.title: Watching as a giant star swallowed its neighbor and exploded
technology.description: In the Andromeda Galaxy, a giant star about seven times as massive as the Sun spent nearly a decade slowly swallowing its much smaller companion. The process, known as common envelope evolution, was proposed in the 1970s to explain how some of the tightest pairs of stars in the Universe form, but no one had ever caught it in the act. In a new Nature study, astronomers led by Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University, finally witnessed the entire spectacle from the decades before it began to the eruption that ended it in late 2025. “It lasts for a few years, maybe a few decades,” Karambelkar said. “Stars evolve on time scales of millions of years. So, it's really like a blip on the entire cosmic time scale.” Shared envelopes Some pairs of stars orbit so close to each other that they could not have formed at that distance, so their orbits must have shrunk. Common envelope evolution is the leading explanation for that shrinkage. When one star in a binary grows old, it expands into a giant, and its outer layers can engulf its companion. The two then share a single, loosely bound envelope of gas. As the engulfed star drags through it, it loses orbital energy to friction and spirals inward. Depending on how much of the envelope gets lost, the pair either ends up in a much tighter orbit or merges. Read full article Comments

science.title: SpaceX launches classified mission for US Space Force from California
science.description: null SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m. EST (8:20 p.m. local California time; 0420 GMT on Nov. 21), on a Space Force mission called USSF-317. The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100. The Falcon 9's first stage rests on the deck of a drone ship after launching the USSF-317 mission. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX ended its launch webcast just after that touchdown, so we didn't get to see the Falcon 9's upper stage power its way to orbit. USSF-317 is a classified mission, so we don't know what the upper stage is carrying or where exactly it's headed. However, some experts think that USSF-317 may be hauling a batch of SpaceX's Starshield satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO) for the Space Force's Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio, which helps the military keep tabs on potential targets around the world. Previous Booster 1100 missions NROL-105 | USSF-385 | 8 Starlink missions USSF-317 was the 121st Falcon 9 launch of 2026 and the third mission that SpaceX has launched for the Space Force so far in November. The vast majority of this year's Falcon 9 missions — about 70% of them — have been devoted to building out SpaceX's Starlink LEO internet constellation, which currently consists of more than 11,000 satellites. The Falcon 9 has been putting up incredible numbers lately — it flew a whopping 165 times in 2025 , for example — but the workhorse rocket is on its way out . science.title: What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental?
science.description: Bernhard Riemann set out a problem mathematicians have been trying solve for more than a century The Granger Collection/Alamy The cadence of prime numbers has a pattern; it isn’t simply chaos. Mathematician Bernhard Riemann suspected this was the case, but he never proved it conclusively, and his mathematical successors have spent more than a century trying to demonstrate that he was right. The Riemann hypothesis may now be proven , and it could reveal the most basic structure of our number system, while also opening the door for a new understanding of the vast world of mathematical functions. Read more Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what’s true In 1859, Riemann made a casual remark about a mathematical function in his memoir, qualifying a statement about it as “very probably” true. The fact that he never proved it more definitively has held the world of mathematics in suspense ever since, and the “Riemann hypothesis” became the field’s most famous and stubbornly unsolved problem – until now. A new AI-assisted proof by Levent Alpöge at Anthropic may have just ended a whole era of mathematics by confirming Riemann’s hunch from nearly 200 years ago. “This result, if true, will be the culmination of a struggle thousands of mathematicians have attempted in the past,” says Christopher Hughes at the University of York in the UK. The proof of the Reimann hypothesis is also one of the Clay Mathematics Institute ’s Millennium Prize Problems, each of which comes with a $1 million prize for a solution. Advertisement The Riemann hypothesis has loomed so large over mathematicians for decades because it concerns mathematics’ most simple yet hard-to-understand objects: prime numbers . These are numbers that aren’t divisible by any number other than 1 and themselves, and any number can be built by multiplying primes. In this way, primes are the bones of all systems of numbers; everything is built on top of them. But how primes are distributed among all numbers is, on the face of it, unpredictable. This is where Riemann made an intervention. He hypothesised that the way primes are spaced throughout the number line can be inferred from another set of numbers, now tied to a mathematical function called the Riemann zeta function. These numbers are complex – so each is actually a pair of numbers, one called real and one called imaginary – and when they are plugged into the Riemann zeta function, the function spits out zero. Confusingly, these numbers that result in a zero from the function are called “non-trivial zeros”. Riemann discovered that summing over a sequence of these complex numbers allowed him to predict the distribution of primes up to a certain high number. Effectively, he came upon a formula that could make sense of primes’ seemingly random appearances among numbers. science.title: Don't turn the moon into the Wild West, scientists warn
science.description:
Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. Originally from Prague, the Czech Republic, she spent the first seven years of her career working as a reporter, script-writer and presenter for various TV programmes of the Czech Public Service Television. She later took a career break to pursue further education and added a Master's in Science from the International Space University, France, to her Bachelor's in Journalism and Master's in Cultural Anthropology from Prague's Charles University. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment. Two such researchers are Florian Rabitz, a professor of climate and technology governance at Vilnius University in Lithuania, and Xiao-Shan Yap, an assistant professor of Earth-space sustainability at Utrecht University in the Netherlands. In a piece published last month in the journal Global Environmental Politics , the pair call for "robust international regulations" and "broad and inclusive deliberation" to allow the global community to carefully consider the impact of economic activities on the moon. In addition to the threat to the scientifically priceless lunar landscape, the researchers also object to the colonization of the moon by a small number of powerful players — namely China, the U.S. and their respective close allies. "With the moon it's absolutely clear that whoever is doing the big infrastructure work is going to be asserting their position, including by defining their own exclusive territories," Rabitz said in a statement . "That shouldn't be the Wild West." Rabitz pointed out that, although the United Nations' 1967 Outer Space Treaty prevents individual nations from appropriating the moon, Earth's natural satellite and its valuable resources are unlikely to remain truly neutral territory if its exploitation is going to be led by a small number of powerful nations.
